question: In 2024, the European Parliament deactivated access cards for Amazon’s interest representatives, following repeated refusals to participate in hearings. On 28 January 2026, Members of the European Parliament once again highlighted Amazon’s lack of cooperation and serious risks to occupational health and safety.

Continued allegations of pressure and discrimination against trade unions at Amazon warehouses have also been reported. What is more, on 16 February 2026, a trade union delegation and members of the press were once again denied access to the site at Senlis, France. In spite of all this, members of the Commission continue to hold regular meetings with Amazon representatives. 1.

What criteria and procedure does the Commission follow to deny, restrict or place conditions on meetings with a company when there are serious and repeated allegations regarding freedom of association, social dialogue and health and safety at work?

Does the Commission undertake to make any future meetings with Amazon conditional upon cooperation in good faith with the EU institutions’ requests for hearings and monitoring? Will it also make them conditional upon verifiable guarantees that freedom of association will be respected and unhindered access to sites will be given to delegations including workers’ representatives and observers?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (4.5.2026) The Commission attaches great importance to respect for fundamental rights, including freedom of association, the right of collective bargaining and action, and fair and just working conditions.

At the same time, the Commission applies strict transparency rules concerning its contacts and interactions with stakeholders on issues relating to EU decision-making and policy implementation. Members of the Commission, members of their Cabinet, and Commission staff holding management functions shall only meet interest representatives that are registered in the Transparency Register1.

Information and minutes of all such meetings are published in accordance with Commission Decisions (EU) 2024/30812 and 2024/30823. Amazon Europe is registered in the Transparency Register. Its registration4 includes information on meetings held with the Commission in an interest representation context.

All registrants commit to operate in line with the rules and principles set out in the code of conduct annexed to the applicable Interinstitutional Agreement5. The register’s Secretariat is tasked with evaluating registrants’ ongoing eligibility and observance of the code of conduct. To that end, it may carry out investigations and apply measures of an administrative nature.

Any natural or legal person may lodge a complaint with the Secretariat concerning a registrant’s alleged non-observance of the code. Amazon Europe’s registration is currently not subject to any administrative measure by the Secretariat.
